HERO.TAGLINE: Scan, understand, with privacy in mind.
HERO.INTRO: A mobile application combining computer vision and language models to help users identify medications and understand prescriptions.

CONTEXT.TITLE: Making medical information easier to understand
CONTEXT.CARD1_TEXT: Handwritten prescriptions can be difficult to read, while medication packaging contains a lot of technical information.
CONTEXT.CARD2_TEXT: One application to scan medication packaging, analyze prescriptions, and ask questions to an assistant.
CONTEXT.CARD3_TEXT: Privacy first: text is extracted on the device, and the language model runs locally.

FEATURES.TITLE: Key features
FEATURES.DESCRIPTION: Each screen is designed to provide a smooth and intuitive experience.
FEATURES.HOME_TEXT: The home screen gives one-tap access to every feature: health chatbot, eye scanner, prescription analysis, medication recognition and nearby open pharmacies.
FEATURES.MEDICINE_TEXT: Users scan a medication package. The application extracts the name and active ingredient, then displays the associated health information.
FEATURES.PRESCRIPTION_TEXT: The application scans the medical document, extracts text using OCR, and organizes it clearly to make the treatment easier to understand.
FEATURES.ASSISTANT_TEXT: A chatbot answers questions in natural language. It uses a locally running language model to provide contextual responses while helping protect data privacy.
FEATURES.EYES_TEXT: Users can take a photo or select an image from the gallery. The application analyzes the eyes and displays the detection results, confidence level, and a risk indication.

TECH.FIREBASE_TEXT: Authentication and data storage services that support rapid prototyping without requiring a complex server to manage.
TECH.OCR_TEXT: On-device text recognition from images to help extract information from scanned documents.
TECH.OLLAMA_TEXT: Running a language model locally can help protect data privacy and avoid recurring API costs.

hero.title: Home Insurance Claim Prediction
hero.intro: Development of a supervised classification approach to predict whether a claim will occur during the insurance period, based on building and policy characteristics.
hero.f1: XGBoost weighted F1-score on test data
hero.coverAlt: Cover image for the home insurance claim prediction project

context.label: 01 · Project context
context.title: Anticipating risks to better protect properties
context.description: This project focuses on predicting home insurance claims. The goal is to use available data to build a model that classifies buildings according to their claim risk.

problem.title: Problem statement
problem.text: How can insurance data be used to better anticipate claims and improve risk assessment?

objective.title: Objective
objective.text: Build and evaluate a robust, high-performing supervised classification model based on building characteristics.

approach.title: Approach
approach.text: Combine exploratory analysis, data preprocessing, feature selection, modelling and validation.

method.label: 02 · Methodology
method.title: From raw data to an evaluated model
method.description: A step-by-step workflow to prepare the data, train the models and analyse their performance.

exploration.label: 03 · Exploration and preprocessing
exploration.title: Preparing reliable data for machine learning
exploration.description: This stage handles missing values, skewed distributions and relationships between features. The charts below illustrate the main operations.

fig1.title: 1. Handling extreme values
fig1.text: The area_m2 variable has a highly skewed distribution. A logarithmic transformation is applied to reduce the influence of large values, followed by quantile-based discretisation.

fig2.title: 2. Analysing Geo_Code
fig2.text: The distribution of Geo_Code is examined before processing. Non-numeric values are converted to missing values and then imputed using KNNImputer with seven neighbours.

fig3.title: 3. Discretisation and clustering
fig3.text: Discretisation of area_m2_log is explored using different numbers of bins. Geo_Code is grouped into five clusters using a GMM model fitted on the training set.

fig4.title: 4. Correlation and feature selection
fig4.text: The correlation matrix is used to examine relationships between features. According to the presented workflow, has_garden, locality and is_fenced are removed before modelling.

exploration.alt1: Area distribution before and after logarithmic transformation
exploration.alt2: Density plot of the Geo_Code variable
exploration.alt3: Histograms used to select discretisation parameters

missing.title: Missing values
missing.text: Some features in the dataset contain missing values.
missing.solution: Solution: process has_garden according to is_finished_and_fenced and use KNNImputer for the relevant variables.

complex.title: Complex features
complex.text: Some information is combined in a single column, while Geo_Code requires specific processing.
complex.solution: Solution: split is_finished_and_fenced and group Geo_Code into five clusters using GMM.

outliers.title: Outliers
outliers.text: Building areas contain extreme values that may influence model training.
outliers.solution: Solution: logarithmic transformation of area_m2 and quantile-based discretisation.

imbalance.title: Imbalanced data
imbalance.text: Observations with and without claims are not evenly distributed.
imbalance.solution: Solution: handle inconsistent duplicates, reduce some duplicates and analyse weighted metrics.

models.label: 05 · Modelling
models.title: Comparing XGBoost and Random Forest
models.description: Two supervised classification algorithms are evaluated to compare their performance and ability to detect observations from the minority class.

compare.title: Model comparison
compare.text: The weighted recall and weighted F1-score favour XGBoost in the results shown. Model selection is based on comparing several metrics.
compare.alt: Comparison of weighted performance metrics for XGBoost and Random Forest

importance.title: Feature interpretation
importance.text: Both models identify area_m2_log_grp as the most important feature. XGBoost then distributes importance across several other features.
importance.alt: Feature importance according to XGBoost and Random Forest

evaluation.label: 06 · Evaluation
evaluation.title: Checking result stability
evaluation.description: The evaluation compares performance on training and test data, then observes how the error changes as the training set grows.

metrics.title: XGBoost weighted metrics
metrics.text: On training and test data, weighted precision is 0.76 and 0.75 respectively, recall is 0.68 and 0.70, and F1-score is 0.71 for both. These values suggest stable metrics across the two sets.
metrics.alt: Comparison of XGBoost weighted metrics on training and test data

learning.title: Learning curve
learning.text: As the number of training examples increases, test error decreases and the two curves move closer together. This suggests improved generalisation and no severe overfitting in this analysis.

evaluation.note: XGBoost reaches a weighted F1-score of 0.71 on the test set. Weighted metrics summarise overall performance; they do not replace a specific analysis of the “claim” class.

conclusion.label: 07 · Project summary
conclusion.title: What I developed through this project
conclusion.description: An end-to-end Data Mining workflow, from data exploration and cleaning to modelling, evaluation and interpretation of results.
conclusion.future1: Integrate climate and natural hazard data
conclusion.future2: Explore an alert system for at-risk buildings

HERO.TITLE: Tech Salary Analytics
HERO.INTRO: A multidimensional analysis of salaries in the technology sector through a complete business intelligence pipeline, from data integration to interactive visualization.

OVERVIEW.LABEL: 01 — OVERVIEW
OVERVIEW.TITLE: Understanding salaries in tech
OVERVIEW.INTRO: Transform raw data into actionable insights through a structured business intelligence architecture.
OVERVIEW.ETL_TEXT: Implementation of an ETL process with SSIS to prepare, transform, and load data into the data warehouse.
OVERVIEW.MODEL_TEXT: Organizing data in a Data Warehouse using a star schema with a fact table and dimensions.
OVERVIEW.OLAP_TEXT: Exploring measures and dimensions through an OLAP cube and MDX queries.
OVERVIEW.DASHBOARD_TEXT: Building a Power BI dashboard to explore salaries by job, experience level, location, and year.

ETL.LABEL: 02 — DATA INTEGRATION
ETL.TITLE: From raw data to the data warehouse
ETL.INTRO: The ETL process prepares and loads the data required for business intelligence analysis.

MODEL.LABEL: 03 — DATA MODELING
